(i) **Full Wave Rectifier Using Center-Tapped Transformer:**
- **Working:** During the positive half cycle of the AC input, diode $D_1$ is forward-biased and conducts, while $D_2$ is reverse-biased. During the negative half cycle, the polarity reverses, making $D_2$ forward-biased and conducting, while $D_1$ is reverse-biased. Current flows through load $R_L$ in the same direction during both half cycles.
- **Derivations:**
  - **Output DC Voltage ($V_{\text{avg}}$):** $V_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2V_m}{\pi}$
  - **AC Output Voltage ($V_{\text{rms}}$):** $V_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_m}{\sqrt{2}}$
  - **Efficiency ($\eta$):** $\eta = \frac{P_{\text{dc}}}{P_{\text{ac}}} = \frac{40.6\%}{(1 + R_f/R_L)} \approx 81.2\%$ (for ideal diode)
  - **Peak Inverse Voltage ($\text{PIV}$):** $\text{PIV} = 2V_m$

---(ii) **Series DC Configuration Analysis:**
Given circuit values: $E_1 = 10\text{ V}$, $R_1 = 4.7\text{ k}\Omega$, Si diode ($V_D = 0.7\text{ V}$), $R_2 = 2.2\text{ k}\Omega$, $E_2 = -5\text{ V}$.

Applying KVL around the loop:
$$E_1 - I R_1 - V_D - I R_2 - E_2 = 0$$
$$10 - I(4.7\text{ k}\Omega) - 0.7 - I(2.2\text{ k}\Omega) - (-5) = 0$$
$$14.3 - I(6.9\text{ k}\Omega) = 0 \implies I = \frac{14.3\text{ V}}{6.9\text{ k}\Omega} = 2.07\text{ mA}$|

- **Current $I$:** $2.07\text{ mA}$
- **Voltage $V_1$ across $R_1$:** $I \times R_1 = 2.07\text{ mA} \times 4.7\text{ k}\Omega = 9.73\text{ V}$
- **Voltage $V_2$ across $R_2$:** $I \times R_2 = 2.07\text{ mA} \times 2.2\text{ k}\Omega = 4.55\text{ V}$
- **Output Voltage $V_o$:** Voltage at the node with respect to ground:
  $$V_o = E_2 + I R_2 = -5 + 4.55 = -0.45\text{ V}$|
proTip: Remember that the PIV for a center-tapped full-wave rectifier is twice the peak secondary voltage ($2V_m$), unlike the bridge rectifier.
